correctness.rationale: Radial integration over an eighth-sector produces area 4tφ; polarity changes intersection to the convex hull of the two reciprocal ellipses, with the first-quadrant boundary made of two congruent elliptic arcs and the common diagonal supporting segment. Green’s formula gives polar area 4φ/t+2(1−t^−2). With t=cotφ, product F(φ)=16(φ²+φ cot2φ), derivative 16 cos2φ(sin2φ−2φ cos2φ)/sin²2φ>0 on 0<φ<π/4, and dφ/dt<0. Taylor coefficients are 4(t−1)² and 16/(3t²). Independent symbolic differentiation/limits and separate radial/support-function quadratures confirmed formulas for t=1,5/4,3/2,2,3,5,10. Analytic geometry covers all real t≥1.

value.rationale: A natural fourfold-symmetric path from the Euclidean disk to the extremal planar square has a complete affine-invariant Mahler product profile. The exact strict interpolation and distinct second-order endpoint rates constitute a useful geometric benchmark that is not a routine equality case of the planar Mahler inequality.

final_claim: For all real t≥1, the intersection of orthogonally oriented concentric ellipses of semiaxes (t,1) has area 4t arctan(1/t), polar area 4 arctan(1/t)/t+2(1−t^(−2)), and strictly decreasing product 16 arctan(1/t)^2+8(t−t^(−1))arctan(1/t), from π² to unattained 8, with both sharp endpoint coefficients.
